diagnosis.statement: The all-center O(R) packet-capacity law contains genuine large-scale volumetric vorticity sparsity, but after normalization at R=a*Omega^(-1/2) the available volume-fraction bound is C I/[a^2 min(a^2,1/chi)], chi=||partial_t omega||_infinity/Omega^2. Finite I and ancient smoothing provide finiteness but not the small dimensionless control needed for O(1) critical-scale sparsity; audited existing consumers also have mismatched input types.

failure.attempted_implication: finite-I ancient NSE packet capacity => existing geometric regularity theorem
failure.supported_failure: The currently registered producer does not source-bind an exact existing consumer: Albritton-Bradshaw requires velocity-Lp sparsity data, Grujic 2011 uses local 1D sparseness, Grujic 2026 requires critical Lorentz vorticity plus direction control upstream, and GKP requires a global critical function space.
nonclaims: No theorem says a finite-I ancient NSE state actually saturates the bad I,chi regime.
No impossibility of geometric regularity routes is proved.
No Type-I singularity is constructed or excluded.

obstruction.statement: A successful route must either control a scale-aligned dimensionless temporal/cascade coordinate such as I*chi, provide a valid volume-to-exact-consumer transformation preserving center/time quantifiers, or identify an alternate same-theory consumer that directly accepts finite-I capacity geometry.

candidate_lesson.statement: After deriving an all-center growth/capacity law, normalize it at the downstream consumer's critical physical scale, expose every surviving dimensionless factor, and type-check geometry/state/time inputs before composing to a regularity theorem. Large-scale sparsity alone is not consumer-scale identification.

motif.pattern: A source-valid local-to-large-scale estimate becomes non-identifying after normalization because a bounded-but-not-small scale-invariant coordinate survives, and the intended consumer has a stricter input type.
